sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Pranjal Mehrotra Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Manish Kumar Nigam,J.
1.

Heard Sri Nawal Kishor Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Pranjal Mehrotra,
learned counsel appearing for N.H.A.I.
2.

The petitioners have prayed for quashing of the notices issued by Competent Authority under Section 3E of National Highways Act, 1956, intimating the affected persons, including the petitioners, that an award has been declared on 16.12.2023 and the petitioners may approach his office for release of the compensation amount.

The petitioners have also prayed for a mandamus Smt. Chinta Devi And 3 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166234641/
1 commanding respondent nos. 2 and 3 to pay compensation at market value of the land as provided under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Standing Counsel has placed on record the written instructions received from the Competent Authority Ballia, according to which notice has been issued to the petitioners to approach him with necessary documents to unable disbursement of compensation to them in terms of the award.
4. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioners is that the amount determined as compensation under the award is inadequate and not as per the circle rate.
5. We are of the opinion that the said issue can be raised by the petitioners by challenging the award as provided under Section 3G(5) of the Act.
6. Counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are unable to avail the said remedy as no Arbitrator has been appointed for District Ballia.

7. Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, learned counsel appearing for N.H.A.I. has placed before us a notification dated 02.07.2024, according to which District Magistrate, Ballia is to act as Arbitrator under Section 3G(5) of the Act.
8. In view of the above, the relief claimed cannot be granted in writ proceedings.
We leave it open to the petitioners to assail the award by seeking arbitration as provided under the Act, if so advised.
9. The writ petition is disposed of, accordingly.
(Manish Kumar Nigam, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 13.8.2024
